newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-UEFA CLAIM ENGLAND KNEW OF WORLD CUP PLAN.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-UEFA CLAIM ENGLAND KNEW OF WORLD CUP PLAN.

text.p: England soccer authorities insisted on Sunday they did not know until last week of the European Football Union's support for a bid by Germany to stage the 2006 World Cup in Germany.
They promised to continue their bid to hold the tournament even though UEFA insisted that their backing of Germany's candidature had been known for two years.
England's case was supported by national coach Glenn Hoddle, who said FIFA Must heed the English bid after the success of Euro '96 last year.
"England's case is a very strong one indeed. Top players from all around the world play here at the moment," Hoddle said.
He added that he was certain players would want to play in a World Cup in England.
"But above all by the year 2006 it will be 40 years since we last hosted a World Cup. How much longer are we expected to wait?"

The FA's spokesman David Davies, insisting England did not know of UEFA's position, said: "The first question must be when and where this was recorded publicly as such a decision would have been an important matter.
"Two years ago it's entirely true there was just one European bid, but now we have bid and there may also be others."
He said UEFA officials had not mentioned the agreement with Germany, even when they were in a perfect position to do so.
England's bid has the full backing of Prime Minister John Major and Labour leader Tony Blair.
UEFA officials have maintained that England's bid was launched after the decision to support Germany had been taken.
UEFA president Lennart Johansson said that for English officials not to have known about the decision, there must have been "a terrible lack of communication".
He said UEFA officials would visit England to clarify the position and added it was up to England to decide what to do, as no one could "hinder" their application.
"It's a long way from here to 2006," he said.
